title: Space tool cockpit and reliable tool connections: per-room MCP enablement, per-binding allowlist, credential mode and scoped consent, health states and person-bound sign-in links
summary: Let a Space manager enable org-approved MCP servers for a room, set a per-binding tool allowlist and choose per-user or shared credentials, with plain-language consent cards bound to the exact Space, agent and tool, by extending the Model Gateway MCP registry (plan items S3.4 and S3.6). Make tool use fail visibly and recover: a per-server health state machine with reconnect and backoff, separate idle and total call budgets, a typed result union with recovery hints (needs_auth, retry_after, fresh schema), a room-visible 'needs sign-in' card, and person-bound OAuth consent links whose callback verifies the signer.
whyItMatters: An MCP registry with shared or per-user credentials is table stakes among the agent references (Grok Bot, buzz, QM). Verevon's registry, OAuth 2.1 and argument validation are good, but nothing is scoped to a Space, so room agents either get no tools or org-wide tools.

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-06-02] MCP registry: 3 of 5 (table-stakes among agent products); container-scoped consent: Teams only (unique) [R-t1-06-08] MCP runtime policy: Grok Bot only (unique); connected apps by consent link: 2 of 5 (grokbot, qm; differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-06-02] qm's server record carries credentialScope shared|per_user (resolved by the runtime from the initiating principal's keychain, never from tool arguments), a toolAllowlist and a readOnly flag; tools reach the model filtered by allowlist and binding policy. Grok Bot adds per-tool permissions and the richest config schema. Teams RSC stores consent per (app, container) by a container owner, uses about 106 plain-language permission strings with _Chat/_Group/_User scope, and intersects token scope with the caller's ACL. [R-t1-06-08] Grok Bot routes URL servers through a backend executor and stdio servers through the box, caches discovery 24 h with background refresh, reconnects fast and periodically with 10 s health probes, bounds calls at 2 min idle and 60 min total, and returns a union success|error|rejected|permission_denied|tool_not_found|server_not_found with typed McpError {needs_auth, retry_after_ms, recovery{fresh_input_schema, available_tools}}. qm stores a consent link {principal, toolkit, return URL, expiry}, completes auth only for the signed-in principal, and checks owner, active status and tool version before every call, never retrying an uncertain execution and excluding arguments from audit.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: [R-t1-06-02] Model Gateway registers, lists, deletes and shares MCP servers (Private/Shared/Org scope, optional allowlist at connect, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration, one auto-detecting connect route). A grep of spaces.rs and src/features/spaces finds no MCP reference: no per-room enablement, no per-binding tool allowlist, no per-user versus shared credential choice, no consent card. Owner agent-action grants exist but only tickets.create is correlated to receipts; per-conversation grants are a stub; the credential broker (S3.4) is planned only. [R-t1-06-08] Spot-check (SRC): Model Gateway validates arguments against the tool schema before the call (equal to Grok Bot's repair), caches tenant MCP discovery with 6 s discovery and 10 s HTTP timeouts, and runs OAuth 2.1 with a server-side callback, which avoids the loopback problem. Not found: reconnect/backoff and health probing, idle versus total call budgets (10 s is short for long tools), typed recovery hints surfaced to the model, per-message MCP config, sandbox-resident stdio servers. integration-corev2 has an org-level OAuth catalogue (Microsoft, Slack, Google, Notion, GitHub, Shopify, Stripe, LinkedIn and more) with PKCE and read actions; missing for Spaces are consent links minted from a room for a given person, per-call owner/status/version evidence and Space credential grants (S3.4).

approachOriginal: [R-t1-06-02] Model Plane (model-gateway / capability-core): add space_ref enablement and a per-binding tool allowlist to the MCP server rows, and resolve credentialScope (shared versus requesting principal) at call time from the requester. Control Plane: generalise owner-grant decisions to (principal or agent, action or tool id, Space ref, expiry, once/session/standing), keep grant mutation on human-only APIs as S3.6 requires, and reuse existing secret stores (S3.4 says do not add a QM-style keychain). Frontend Agent tab: list org-activated servers, enable per room, show health and last use with a revoke action, and render a Teams-style consent card in the room the first time an agent needs a tool. Never grant more than the org activated or the server owner shared. Phase 1 (enablement, allowlist, credential scope) is M; consent cards and the cockpit view are the rest. [R-t1-06-08] Model Plane model-gateway: per-server health state machine with backoff, separate idle and total timeouts per tool, a typed error union with recovery hints returned to the model, and honouring Retry-After. Frontend: a 'needs sign-in' card in the room linking to the existing server-side OAuth flow, plus health shown in the Space cockpit (this item (R-t1-06-02)). Ingestion Plane integration-corev2: person-bound consent links with a callback that checks the signed-in principal, per-call checks of owner, status and version, no retry when an outcome is uncertain, arguments excluded from audit. Control Plane grants tie a connection to a Space binding. Stdio MCP servers run only inside the Space sandbox once S3.2 lands. The Model proposes provider actions and Ingestion executes them after the authority check.

risks: [R-t1-06-02] A shared credential lets any room member act as its owner (needs an explicit warning and a read-only default); consent fatigue and grant sprawl without expiry; a private MCP server must not be widened by Space linkage. [R-t1-06-08] Retry storms against third-party servers (respect Retry-After); wrong-person binding via forwarded links; over-broad OAuth scopes; non-idempotent calls retried after an uncertain outcome.

title: Agents and AI answers over room history under the asker's authority: search_space_history and open_space_entry tools, cited answers over messages and Space knowledge
summary: Give room agents search_space_history and open_space_entry tools on a new capability, backed by the Session Core index, each call running under the Control decision of the human who triggered the turn (never an agent-wide grant), with a rule that stops an agent quoting member-private results into the shared room. On top, let a question in Space search produce a generated answer with linked citations (entry deep links and documents) composed from Data Plane retrieval and message search under the asker's decision, plus an 'Ask agent about this' message action.
whyItMatters: Agents cannot read room history beyond the current transcript, and grounded answers cover documents and wiki only. Slack and QM show the safe pattern (search as the asking human, references not copies); Verevon's signed decisions are a stronger primitive than Slack's action token.

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-04-03] 3 of 5 sources for the history tool (common); 2 of 5 for delegated-authority search (differentiator) [R-t1-04-06] 2 of 5 sources; differentiator (buzz has no AI answers)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-04-03] qm sessions.search returns {sessionId, entry seq} references without widening read access; the history tool does an all-terms keyword search or reopens one entry by seq, including content compacted out of context. GrokBot adds scopes (this chat, earlier, everything) and a prompt rule to trust the newest result and ask when results conflict. Slack Real-time Search mints an action token from the triggering event with per-content scopes, limits results to what the user can access, and forbids storing results. [R-t1-04-06] A question-shaped query triggers hybrid keyword plus semantic retrieval restricted to content the asker can access (files, canvases, clip transcripts, connected docs); top passages go to the model with citation ids and the answer renders with linked citations above the normal results. Teams adds channel citations and a select-text "Ask Copilot" hand-off with prefilled prompts (summarise, flag decisions, help me reply).

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: [R-t1-04-03] Agents have knowledge_search (cap.retrieval.query over Data Plane documents) but no tool that searches or reopens room or thread history; a grep of execution-core in this step found no search_space or space_history symbol. Signed Control decisions (subject, Space, audience, 2-minute lifetime, payload digest) already exist for grounded document retrieval, but there is no equivalent decision for message-history search and no rule against quoting a member's private results into the room. Whether Space room turns offer knowledge_search at all was not confirmed. [R-t1-04-06] Grounded room turns (policy-gated retrieval) exist, but retrieval covers Space-bound documents and wiki only, not room messages or agent outputs. There is no answer-in-search surface for Space content (the gateway search/answer/stream route is the web-search answer path) and no select-text hand-off. The comparator reports Space knowledge as empty in practice because no import writes space_ref; this step found a Space import chain in code (gateway personal_import_ingress_decision, Control personal_import_decision.go, documents-api space_import.go verifying the decision), so whether Space documents are actually populated is unconfirmed.

approachOriginal: [R-t1-04-03] Model Plane execution-core: add the two tools, register them in capability_policy.rs next to knowledge_search and in binding allowed_tools, add a system-prompt snippet (prefer newest, cite thread_id+seq, ask when two results conflict, treat retrieved messages as data). They call Session Core SearchSpaceMessages with the turn decision. Control Plane: issue a search decision for the invoking subject per turn, and define the rule when several humans trigger one run (intersection of authorities is safest). Add an output filter that blocks posting hits marked private into a shared Space. Exclude ZDR turns. [R-t1-04-06] Model Plane composes the answer: two tools (Data Plane retrieval, Session Core message search) called with the asker's Control decision, grounded-answer prompt requiring citation ids, citations rendered as deep links via F-t1-018 (R-t1-04-02). Reuse the existing retrieval policy bit (retrieval_read_entitled) and keep its degrade-to-ungrounded behaviour on 403. Frontend: answer card above search results and a message action "Ask agent about this". Index agent outputs only where ZDR allows.

verevon.constraints: The message index must live in Session Core (Model Plane); no other plane reads its tables. Reuse the model.thread.read Control decision for search rather than a new decision type, and note that today only retrieval and space decision tokens travel in space_context, so an in-run history tool needs a short-lived read decision added at run start or a fresh Control call. title: Entry references and permalinks: one entity router for message, thread and run links, deep links honoured, Space-role pins, visibility-preserving fork, quote and forward
summary: Introduce one reference to a room entry (space_ref, thread_id, seq) that the server resolves under the viewer's audience revision, and one SPA route table of (entity, action) pairs with /spaces/:id/m/:entry and /spaces/:id/runs/:run; notification clicks, push actions, agent-posted links and protocol/share handlers all call it, and message links page back until the target is loaded. Build pins by Space role (lifted above the timeline, capped, pinnable by an agent), a Session Core fork that copies only what the forking viewer can see, quoted replies with tombstones, and forward with a decision per destination.
whyItMatters: Deep links are table stakes in four references. Activity already emits ?thread_id links that SpacePage ignores, pins are author-only flags that are not lifted, and fork is an open S1.7 checkbox; one router avoids every surface inventing its own link handling.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: buzz (entity link chips and deep links); qm (visibility-preserving fork, capped surface-neutral pins); slack and teams (header shelf, quote with tombstone, forward); teams (toast clicks, deep links and lifecycle events normalised into one (entity, action) command) with qm (?seq= pages older history until the target message is loaded and highlights it)
others: slack (maps the team in a link to a workspace the user belongs to; holds links until the web app is ready)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-01-11] Pins 3 of 5 (common); deep links, fork, quoted replies and forward each 2 of 5 (differentiators) [R-t1-11-03] 4 of 5 sources (slack, grokbot, qm, teams) = table-stakes.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-01-11] Deep link: URL scheme /spaces/{ref}/t/{thread}/e/{seq}; the router opens the exact entry; known hosts render as chips; external crawlers get minimal metadata. Pins: room_pins(room, entry_seq or note, pinned_by, at) capped (409 pin_limit), room editor and above, shown in the header and info pane. Fork: fork(thread, upto_seq) reads the viewer-folded transcript (or the intersection across members under a roster lock), appends copies to a fresh thread and records forkedFrom and forkBoundarySeq. Quote: the message carries quoted_message_id plus a server-resolved snapshot; on render it re-resolves and shows a tombstone or a cannot-verify marker. Forward: a new entry with a forwarded_from chip and size and count validation; access to the source is rechecked. [R-t1-11-03] Route table of entity types x actions; resolver checks membership before navigating and fails closed; message links load the transcript window around the target id then scroll and highlight; notifications reuse the exact same command object.

Pin is a thread-level flag that only the post's author can set, and the timeline re-sorts chronologically so pins are flagged, not lifted; no pinned section, bookmark shelf or agent pin (room-wide pin by non-authors is a known open item in the page audit). Reply targets a thread, not a quoted entry. No forward. Fork is listed as open work in S1.7 and has no code. [R-t1-11-03] Space plus tab is linkable (/spaces/:spaceId with hash tabs, replaceState on tab change). Chat has a validated /chat?thread_id= deep link that resolves through the owner-bound transcript route (fail-closed parser; a good pattern to copy). No message/entry permalink, agent-run link inside a Space or shared command router exists (grep for permalink, messageId=, ?message= finds nothing); notifications carry a free-form href string rather than a typed route.

approachOriginal: [R-t1-01-11] Frontend: SpacePage reads thread and entry params and scrolls to the entry; entry chips; a minimal, ZDR-aware metadata endpoint for external unfurls that never reveals private titles. Application Plane: room_pins (Space-role authorization, not thread owner; cap with a typed refusal) plus an agent tool to pin; fix the timeline ordering so pinned posts are lifted. Model Plane Session Core: fork RPC built on the existing audience-revision filtering (grpc.rs:5340-5360), copying only rows the forking viewer, or all current members, can see and recording forked_from and boundary_seq; entry field quoted_entry_seq resolved reader-side with a tombstone; forward creates a new entry with provenance and carries no source-room retrieval grants. Every resolution checks the viewer's audience revision first. [R-t1-11-03] Frontend Plane: a typed route builder/reader module (modelled on chat-thread-deep-link.ts) used by the Solid router, notifications, push and agent-posted links; add the two Space routes in App.tsx. Server side comes from this item (R-t1-01-11) (stable (space_ref, thread_id, seq) reference resolved under the viewer audience revision) and an Application Plane read-around-entry call; the resolver never widens an owner-plane ACL, and unfurls expose no titles before the ACL check. Notification payloads should carry entity refs, not hrefs.

title: Per-thread serialized, leased agent run queue and member-safe mid-run steering for multi-member rooms
summary: Verify first, then build: write a test where two members post to the same thread while a turn is running, and confirm what Session Core and execution-core do. Then add a per-thread run claim (at most one running run per thread, lease with heartbeat, reaper that requeues or parks after repeated crashes) and a tool ledger keyed by (run, attempt, call index) so replays do not repeat side effects. Extend the existing mid-run queued input from the Chat path to Space turns so another member's message becomes a steer or a follow-up at the next tool-round boundary, with stop still aborting.
whyItMatters: In a room several people and agents can talk to the same thread at once, so concurrent turns, lost steering and duplicated effects are real correctness risks, not edge cases. QM shows the pattern for serialization and crash recovery; Verevon already has model-classified steering for single-user Chat that is not yet wired into Spaces.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: QM (unique one-running-per-session index, SKIP LOCKED claim, lease heartbeat at ttl/3, abort after 3 lost beats, reaper with crash-loop parking, ToolLedger; routeWake returning engage, steer or drop with a durable RunSignalStore)
others: Grok Bot (Temporal-based durable harness as an alternative)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 5 for a durable per-conversation run queue (differentiator); 1 of 5 for mid-run steering (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: runs table (session_id, status, lease_token, lease_expires_at); claim = UPDATE ... WHERE id = (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) guarded by a unique partial index on (session_id) WHERE status = running; worker heartbeats; reaper requeues expired leases and parks after N crashes; effectful tool calls go through once(runId, attempt, callIndex) which returns the cached result on replay. Incoming message for a thread with a running run is classified engage, steer or drop; steer is appended to a signal store read at step boundaries; unconsumed steers start a follow-up run.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: SRC verified for steering: model-gateway has mid-run queued input delivered at a tool-round boundary, where the model classifies redirect versus follow-up, keyed by request_id and bound to the tenant and user, in-memory and single-replica (its own note says multi-replica needs a NATS subject keyed by request id). It is wired into the Chat page and controller but no reference was found in src/features/spaces. Stop is shipped in the Space composer. Per-thread run serialization, leases and a reaper in Session Core or execution-core were not found by grep (only FOR UPDATE row locks on threads and runs), so concurrent-turn behaviour is unknown.

approachOriginal: Model Plane. (1) Characterise current behaviour with a two-member concurrency test. (2) Session Core / execution-core: per-thread run claim with lease, heartbeat and reaper, plus a tool ledger keyed by Quarry execution receipts for effectful actions. (3) Steering: promote queued_input from request-id to run-id keyed signals stored durably or routed over a NATS subject to the replica holding the stream; gateway route for Space steer gated by a fresh Control append decision per message so each steer is attributed and audited; extend SpaceRoomComposer so a member can send while a turn runs (queued, steer) instead of being locked. Coordinate with F-t1-032 (R-t1-01-08) which plans queue-and-steer in the composer.
risks: Queueing changes perceived latency in busy rooms and needs steering to feel right. Steer text needs its own append decision and audit, and a policy for who may steer another member's turn (queued_input is bound to the requesting user today). Do not widen owner-plane ACLs through the steer path.

verevon.exactGap: Mid-run steering is already built end to end and is Space-aware, except for the Space composer: model-gateway POST /v1/invoke/:request_id/queue accepts a fresh space_append_context and persists the queued message under a Control append decision, the BFF queue route mints that decision through inject_personal_thread_context, and the Chat controller already passes spaceRef; SpaceRoomComposer never calls queueInvocationInput and simply refuses to send while submitting. The registry is bound to the requesting (org, user), in-memory and single-replica, so another member cannot steer a run today. No per-thread run gate exists: session-core start_run_inner inserts a run with ON CONFLICT (id) only, so two members' turns on one thread both run; the only leases are the managed-run heartbeat and recovery worker (marks outcome_unknown after 15 minutes, never requeues) and the approval-delivery outbox, and effect idempotency already rests on owner-plane receipts, so a (run, attempt, call index) ledger has nothing to replay because interactive runs cannot restart.

Chat controller deliverMidRun and QueuedInputStrip as the pattern for SpaceRoomComposer
session-core managed-run terminalization (heartbeat, lease, recovery loop) as the reaper foundation
scheduled_step_receipts and approval-delivery idempotency keys as the effect ledger
Space thread projection poll and working indicator already shown to other members
verevon.constraints: Each steer needs its own fresh Control thread:append decision, which the BFF queue route already mints; queued input is bound to the requesting user, so letting another member steer a run is a policy decision about authority and must not widen any owner-plane ACL. ZDR tokens are refused on the queue route (durable mutation), so ZDR Spaces cannot steer. The interactive turn is pinned to one model-gateway SSE stream, so multi-replica steering needs routing by request id over NATS and a QM-style claim queue is a different architecture: a per-thread guard belongs at session-core run start or as a gateway 409. Model proposes, Quarry executes is unaffected.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Reduce the item to: (a) a two-member concurrency characterisation test, including whether session-core's assistant-reply slot rule (last message must be a user turn) refuses the second reply when two user turns precede it (INF, medium confidence, depends on which append path persists the reply); (b) a per-thread active-run guard at session-core start_run, or a queued-turn state, plus a visible 'agent is busy' state; (c) wire SpaceRoomComposer to the existing queue route for the run owner, then allow member steering by explicit policy (coordinate with F-t1-032); (d) reuse managed-run recovery as the reaper and extend it to requeue or park only once restartable continuations exist. Drop the (run, attempt, call index) tool ledger for now.
verevon.effortNote: Overall L stands, but composer wiring alone is S, the per-thread guard M, cross-replica steering M, and the policy for member steering M. The ledger drops out.
verevon.verdictReason: The text says Space steering is not wired and proposes a gateway route and per-message append decision that already exist; it also proposes a tool ledger that has no restart path to protect. The true gaps are the composer, a per-thread gate and a steer policy.

title: One command layer on the typed action registry: Cmd/Ctrl+K palette and quick switcher, platform slash commands, shortcut sheet, then a unified 'To:' picker
summary: Wrap the typed ActionDescriptor registry plus navigation commands in one command registry {id, title, hotkey, when, run} with a single key handler, Ctrl/Cmd+1-9 Space switching and a '?' shortcut sheet. Rebuild Cmd/Ctrl+K as a palette with fuzzy match over rooms, threads, agents, people and human-eligible actions (web search becomes a palette mode). Add a platform section to the '/' picker (invite, mute, pin, schedule, summarise, pause agent) executed through the same dispatcher and answered ephemerally, then message actions that hand a message to a room agent. Once DMs and a directory exist, add a 'To:' field that finds or creates agents, people and groups.
whyItMatters: Cmd/Ctrl+K opens web search today and '/' lists skills only. Verevon's typed action registry, shared by human clicks and model-initiated actions, is a base no reference has: one vocabulary for people and agents.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: qm; grokbot (every shell action is a registered command with id and hotkey, consumed by one hotkey layer and a mod+K palette); Slack for the keyboard model (switcher, unread navigation, All-unreads, F6 section cycling); Grok Bot for hold-to-reveal hints and the "To:" picker; teams
others: teams (user-assignable shortcuts, slash menu as palette)
qm (hold Cmd to reveal 1-9 session shortcuts)
Teams and Buzz almost certainly ship quick switchers (INF; no records)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-04-04] 3 of 5 sources; common [R-t1-11-05] 4 of 5 sources (buzz, grokbot, teams, qm) = table-stakes; palette itself in 2 of 5. [R-t1-12-07] switcher 2 of 5 in records (Slack, Grok Bot; common, under-counted); "To:" picker 1 of 5 (Grok Bot; unique) [R-t1-06-05] Slash commands: 3 of 5 (table-stakes); message actions and unfurl: Teams only (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-04-04] A global hotkey opens an overlay; input is debounced 150 ms and ignored under 2 characters; two parallel requests (conversation entries, resources) render as groups ordered by recency; Enter navigates or executes. Commands come from a typed registry {id, title, hotkey, run, when} so the palette and the shortcuts share one source (GrokBot has 17 command ids with hotkeys). [R-t1-11-05] Command registry {id, label, hotkey, when, run}; one keydown handler resolves hotkeys (capture phase for globals); a palette fuzzy-searches commands and entities (Spaces, people, agents); custom bindings stored per user. [R-t1-12-07] A global keydown router with scope (app, room, composer) and conflict rules; a palette component with fuzzy match over a combined directory; unread navigation iterates the cross-room unread list; hold-to-reveal arms a ~500 ms timer on modifier keydown, cancelled by other modifiers, keyup or blur, then shows numeric badges bound to Ctrl+1..9. Picker: a recipient token input over agents, team agents and people, free text offers "Create <name> agent", more than one recipient creates a group conversation. [R-t1-06-05] A command registry {name, description, args schema, owner platform|app, visibility}; composer autosuggest merges built-ins, app commands and recents (Teams has the richest built-in set); Slack defines the invocation contract (trigger_id, response_url, ephemeral versus in-channel response). Teams message actions are a context-menu entry posting the message to the app; unfurling registers a domain and the app returns an expandable card preview on paste.

apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/chat/lib/use-chat-shortcuts.ts:11 and apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/components/SpaceCockpit.tsx:170-179 (composer keys and tablist arrows only)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/shared/actions/ActionCommand.tsx:1-40 (typed action registry that can feed the palette)
verevonTodayOriginal.gap: [R-t1-04-04] Cmd/Ctrl+K opens the top web search (CoreNavbar.tsx:122, use-chat-shortcuts.ts:11). ActionCommand is a per-button component, not a palette, and there is no jump-to-room, agent or thread overlay. [R-t1-11-05] Basic keys exist (roving tablist focus, picker arrows, Enter to send), and Cmd/Ctrl+K plus "/" open web search with Escape closing overlays. There is no Space quick switcher, no command registry or palette, no shortcut help sheet and no custom bindings. [R-t1-12-07] No room, thread or agent switcher, no unread jumping and no shortcut hints; creation is three separate flows and there are no people search, DMs or group DMs, so there is no single entry point. Add a command shape {id, title, hotkey, when} to the registry so shortcuts and palette share one source. Message hits join when F-t1-018 (R-t1-04-01) ships. [R-t1-11-05] Frontend Plane: a registry module that adapts shared/actions descriptors (id, label, risk, requiresApproval, zod schemas) and navigation commands; replace the ad-hoc keydown handlers in CoreNavbar.tsx and the Space cockpit with the one layer; execution of any action goes through the existing ActionCommand preview/approval path so authority stays in the owning plane (approval-required actions never run straight from the palette). Move web search into the palette as a provider (coordinate with this item (R-t1-04-04)) and share Ctrl/Cmd+1-9 org switching with F-t1-055 (R-t1-02-12). [R-t1-12-07] Frontend Plane. Phase 1 (S): extend the existing overlay shell into a palette fed by the rooms/threads/agents lists and human-eligible registry actions, fixing its keyboard model (trap, restore, listbox with arrows and Enter) per the UI/UX audit, and rebind Cmd/Ctrl+K with web search as a mode. Phase 2 (M): the "To:" picker over the Control roster (people) and Application agent bindings; creation still runs the two-step Application -> Control lifecycle and renders as pending, with born-narrow agent policy unchanged. [R-t1-06-05] Frontend Plane: populate a command section from the action registry (each action already has a zod schema and risk level), reuse the shared keyboard picker used by @ and /, execute via the existing dispatcher so audit and authority are identical, and render ephemeral results locally. Keep the structured skill_ids contract for skills. Message actions and unfurl follow F-t1-026 (R-t1-06-04) cards; unfurl fetches through Quarry honouring egress and ZDR.

risks: [R-t1-04-04] Rebinding Cmd+K changes existing web-search muscle memory; the palette must not list actions the viewer cannot perform. [R-t1-11-05] Rebinding Cmd/Ctrl+K changes an existing habit (web search); browser-reserved shortcuts collide; model-ineligible and human-only actions must stay filtered. [R-t1-12-07] Shortcut conflicts with the browser and the existing Cmd/Ctrl+K web-search habit; creating agents too casually (keep born-narrow policy and the human-only creation path). [R-t1-06-05] Name collisions between skills and commands (namespace them); SSRF and privacy of previewed URLs for unfurl; commands must not bypass approval on high-risk actions.

verevon.exactGap: A Cmd/Ctrl+K and bare '/' overlay already exists (CoreNavbar.tsx:122-132, 463), but it is a knowledge search over Data Plane retrieval plus a client-side title filter over local chat history, not web search; its results are plain buttons with no focus trap, arrow keys or Enter handling (UI_UX_AUDIT:71, no ArrowDown handler in CoreNavbar.tsx). There is no command registry, Space/room/agent quick switcher, shortcut sheet, number-key room switching or platform slash commands: the Space composer's '/' opens a skill picker only (SpaceRoomComposer.tsx:272). The 'To:' picker has nothing to find because the gateway accepts only personal|room Spaces (spaces.rs:2873), so no DM or group-DM kind and no people directory exist.

ActionDescriptor registry (id, label, description, risk, requiresApproval, zod inputSchema; 14 spaces.* actions) as the action source, executed only through ActionCommand preview then execute and the gateway dispatcher
SpaceRoomComposer listbox picker (role=listbox, aria-activedescendant, arrow/Enter/Tab/Escape) as the keyboard-model reference
DashboardComposer BUILTIN_COMMANDS and matchDraftCommand shape (name, aliases, description, builtin) as the only existing slash-command catalogue
listSpaces, getSpaceThreads, getSpaceRoster, getAgentInstallations clients and space-live-work.ts live/unread store as palette sources
verevon.constraints: Phase 1 is Frontend-only and safe: every source is an existing Control-gated gateway read, so the palette cannot widen what a viewer already sees. Actions must go through ActionCommand/the gateway dispatcher so audit and approval stay with the owning plane, and requiresApproval actions never run directly from the palette. model-eligibility.ts is a separate execution-claim allowlist (empty by default), so 'human-eligible' is simply every registry entry; filter by risk/requiresApproval instead, and note most spaces.* actions need arguments (spaceRef, memberId) that a palette must prompt for. Recent-item history in the palette must obey isLocalRetentionAllowed (ZDR). Thread search is limited to titles/previews already fetched; message search does not exist (F-t1-018). The 'To:' phase is blocked until a DM/group kind and people directory exist in Control/Application.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Correct the premise: Cmd/Ctrl+K opens knowledge search plus local chat history, not web search (web search lives in the Home search panel); keep both groups as palette providers instead of 'moving web search'. Ship the switcher (rooms, threads of loaded rooms, agents, roster people) and the missing keyboard model first. ActionDescriptor has no hotkey or when field, so add them in a thin command wrapper rather than mutating the registry; execute registry actions only where input is derivable (mark_read, set_agent_state for the current room) or after a schema-driven argument prompt. Split the 'To:' picker into its own blocked item behind DMs.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged for phases 1-2 (palette, switcher, keyboard model, shortcut sheet, a few platform slash commands). The To: picker is a separate XL that is blocked on a DM kind and directory, and arg-prompting for registry actions adds work if included.
verevon.verdictReason: The gap is real (no palette, switcher, shortcut sheet or platform commands) but the item misdescribes what Cmd/Ctrl+K opens today and bundles a To: picker that cannot be built yet.

title: Read state, presence and personal follow-ups: per-thread read frontier, mark unread, global presence and agent availability, saved items, reminders and snooze
summary: Extend the room-level read marker into a per-thread server-side read frontier with mark-unread, a first-unread divider and jump-to-first-unread, and opt-in read receipts that degrade in large rooms. Add global presence and status (online, away, do-not-disturb, custom text with expiry) and agent availability derived from run state. Add saved items and a reminder primitive {owner, not_before, sealed target ref, note} with presets, firing into the Home Reminders slice; snooze reuses it and humans can ask an agent to 'ping me at 9 if X is still open'. Store references only so ZDR rooms stay content-free.
whyItMatters: Per-thread read state is table stakes in four references and reminders in three; Verevon has a good durable room-level marker but nothing finer, and no reminders outside support tickets.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: buzz (server-side read frontier with manual-unread overrides); teams (optimistic mark-read and richest availability model); Buzz (privacy-preserving design); Teams for shared room reminders
others: Teams (reminders visible to all room members)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-01-09] Read state 4 of 5 sources (table-stakes); presence 3 of 5 (common); saved items and reminders 2 of 5; urgent re-notify 1 of 5 (unique) [R-t1-05-09] 3 of 5 sources; table-stakes
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-01-09] read_frontier(subject, room, thread, last_read_seq) lives server-side; unread is every entry with seq above the frontier; manual unread moves the frontier back; the client marks optimistically and batches network calls (about 3 per 8 s); receipts are cut off above about 20 participants. Presence is a lease: a heartbeat every 60 s sets a key with a 180 s TTL, OS idle moves to away, a manual status carries text, emoji, expiry and availability, and DND suppresses notifications. Saved items carry a due date and a reminder scheduler; Urgent messages re-notify every N minutes for M minutes until read. [R-t1-05-09] Buzz encrypts the reminder target and note to the author and leaves only a not_before time public, so the server can schedule without knowing what it is about; due reminders surface under Needs action and can wake agents. The reminder id is at least 128 bits of randomness and status is pending, done or cancelled. Teams adds shared room reminders where anyone can delete for all.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: [R-t1-01-09] Room-level lastReadAt marker only (durable and cross-device, which is good); no per-thread frontier, no jump-to-first-unread, no mark-unread, no receipts. Presence is room-scoped online/typing/offline with a 30 s TTL and polling; no global status, away, DND, custom status, or agent working/waiting states. No saved items or reminders in Space. Whether notification-core supports priority re-notify was not verified. [R-t1-05-09] No Space or message reminders. Greps found snooze only for support tickets (InboxPage snoozed_until), ticket follow-up in conversation-core, and the org-deletion reminder notification; nothing in src/features/spaces, capability-core or convex-core. capability-core already has Space-scoped schedules with Control decisions that could host the due-time trigger.

approachOriginal: [R-t1-01-09] Application Plane (Convex): add a per-thread last_read_seq to spaceReadMarkers (schema.ts:845); gateway read route (spaces.rs:1894-1916) takes thread and seq; client marks optimistically and batches; Frontend adds the divider and jump. Presence: a global per-subject presence lease and status table (content-free rows, own-row writes only, kept from the current design), agent availability projected from Model Plane run state; DND honored by notification-core. Later phase: per-user saved_items (access rechecked on read) with reminders through Control schedules; an escalation policy in notification-core for approval-wait entries. Coordinate with category 05 (C-t1-05-007, 013, 019), category 07 (C-t1-07-017) and category 09 (C-t1-09-014) so one presence and unread model is built. [R-t1-05-09] Application Plane: store reminders with refs only; fire due items via the capability-core scheduler or a notification-core delayed job; due items enter the inbox Reminders slice (F-t1-009 (R-t1-05-03)) and respect DND (F-t1-059 (R-t1-05-06)). Frontend Plane: a reminder menu on messages and threads, snooze on inbox items. Add an agent-callable action in the registry so an agent can create a reminder for its owner within explicit grants.
dependencies: F-t1-001 (R-t1-01-01) shared threads (per-thread unread needs them)
Model Plane run-state feed for agent availability
capability-core scheduler or notification-core delayed job
planeOwner: Application Plane (convex-core read state, presence, reminders) with Model Plane (run-state feed)
risks: [R-t1-01-09] Read receipts and presence reveal behavior, so make receipts opt-in and keep presence content-free. Saved references must re-check access when read. Notification fatigue from urgent re-notify. [R-t1-05-09] Shared room reminders need an owner and delete rule; agent-created reminders need a cap so they cannot be used to spam a person.

verevon.exactGap: A durable, cross-device room-level read marker exists (Convex spaceReadMarkers, POST /spaces/{ref}/read, per-post 'New' badges derived against an arrival snapshot), but it was deliberately designed per room and not per thread (spaceReadMarkers.ts:4-12), the marker never moves backwards (advanceMarker), and there is no mark-unread, first-unread divider, jump-to-unread or receipts. Presence is room-scoped online/typing with a 30 s TTL and 8 s typing decay; the only global status is a manual profile availability value in user-core (online/busy/away/offline, no text or expiry) that no Space surface reads, and agent 'working' is only inferred in the browser from the polled thread projection. There are no Space saved items or reminders: only a personal Inbox follow-up and note calendar stored as user settings with no due-time trigger, and a 24 h snooze for support tickets.
reuse: Convex spaceReadMarkers table and the Application-owned own-row, content-free pattern; the SpacePage arrival snapshot and per-post 'New' flag for a first-unread divider and jump
Convex spacePresence heartbeat-with-TTL rows for status extension, and the user-core profile availability field as the home for status text and expiry
Convex ctx.scheduler.runAfter plus the outbox/lease pattern as the due-time trigger for refs-only reminders
notification-core feed (read, seen, archive) as the Inbox Reminders delivery surface
space-live-work.ts working-state derivation until a Model Plane run-state feed exists
capability-core Space-scoped cron schedules only for 'ask an agent to ping me if X is open' (an agent-authored scheduled run)
verevon.constraints: Read state and presence are Application-owned workspace projections and must stay content-free (timestamps against ids). The room marker was chosen over a per-thread frontier on purpose because the room renders every thread inline; a per-thread frontier only pays off once shared multi-turn threads exist (dependency F-t1-001), so do not build it first. Global status spans organisations, so it cannot live in a per-org Convex presence row without leaking; extend the Control profile value or keep org-scoped own-row writes. Agent availability needs an event or API feed from Model Plane (no cross-plane DB reads). Plain reminders should be Application-owned refs-only records fired by the Convex scheduler: capability-core schedules fire Model runs and every fire needs a Control schedule-fire decision, and an agent-created reminder for its owner is an owner action in the S2 sense (only tickets.create is supported today). Reminder target refs must be rechecked for access when the reminder fires. space-defenition.md lists presence polish among non-goals.

Defer per-thread frontiers and receipts until shared threads exist, and drop the unverified 'priority re-notify' claim (notification-core has no priority, urgent or delayed-delivery concept).

title: Room moderation: report, queue, tombstones, user block, and timeout or ban that also stops the person's agents
summary: Add a Report action on every room message (human or agent-authored), a private moderation queue for owners and managers, and signed moderation actions (dismiss, delete with a visible tombstone, timeout, remove, ban) that notify the reporter and the author. Add a per-user block list. Control refuses to issue decisions for a suspended member and for agents owned by a suspended member, and the suspension event drops live subscriptions and in-flight runs.
whyItMatters: Rooms that mix humans and agents need a way to remove harmful or leaked content, including agent output, and to stop a misbehaving participant. Without it Spaces cannot be opened to larger teams or guests. Because personal agents act like humans, a ban that does not cascade to the person's agents becomes a bypass.

slack and teams moderation controls exist in the products but were not recorded in this category
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Moderation workflow: 2 of 5 (buzz, teams); ban cascade to owned agents: 1 of 5 (buzz). Differentiator.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A reports table (target, reporter hidden from the author, reason, status open/processing/resolved/dismissed/escalated) feeds an admin queue grouped by target. Actions are signed commands that write a tombstone visible in the room and notify everyone affected. A per-user block list filters delivery. The ban verdict is checked at authentication for the principal and for its owner (agent to owner link), fails closed on error, and audits which principal matched; a timeout is a write-deny until expires_at and a ban disconnects all sessions.

title: Credential custody and outward actions: secrets broker, per-person connectors, draft-first sends, bounded cross-room reach
summary: Give room agents the ability to use credentials without ever seeing them: a broker in the Ingestion Plane that attaches secrets server-side with host/method/path pinning, https only and no redirects, a one-time secret-drop form that bypasses chat and the model, and Control grants (once|session|standing) bound to the Space audience. On top of that: per-person connector accounts for room agents, draft-first outbound messages where the human stays the sender, bounded cross-room posts under the initiating human's membership, and classification of gateway actions as human-only or agent-callable with a parity test.
whyItMatters: A computer or browser without credentials cannot do real work, and with raw credentials it is a leak risk. Verevon has already decided the design (reuse Control grants and existing connector stores, broker server-side) but none of it is built, so agents cannot yet act on behalf of a person in mail, calendar or SaaS tools from a room.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: qm (broker, secret drop, cross-person asks, reach, route classification); grokbot (shared plugin with per-person OAuth, vault UX, draft cards)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Secrets custody 3 of 5 (common); connectors/plugins for room agents 3 of 5 (common); agent operates product via same API 3 of 5 (common); draft-first outbound 2 of 5 (differentiator); cross-room reach 1 of 5 (unique); credential asks 1 of 5 (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: QM broker: the sandbox sends {credential slug, method, url}; the broker checks capability claims, host, method and decoded path prefix, uses redirect:manual, caps responses at 5 MB and writes an audit receipt; secret drop is a platform-styled one-time form with a random drop id, peek/redeem once and 7-day expiry; KeychainAsk/Grant {mode once|standing, audienceScopeId, expiry, revokedAt}. Grok Bot plugin {mcp_config, skills, variable_names, connector_type USER|TEAM} with per-person OAuth accounts and install modes OPTIONAL|DEFAULT|REQUIRED. Drafts: Draft {from,to,cc,subject,body} or {workspace,target,thread,body}, SendDraft/DiscardDraft, setting always|needs-approval|disabled. QM reach: resolveReachTarget(recipient|channel|participants) -> not_a_member|identity_unverified|ambiguous|group_too_large with at most 5 cross-conversation posts per turn. QM route table: agentApiMatches() gates paths per capability token and a parity test pins which routes an agent token can call.

title: Agent runtime guardrails for shared rooms: member-text screening, shell command policy, room approvals, secret masking, DLP
summary: Extend the existing screening and policy code to what other people put into a room. (a) Add a trust class for non-owner room messages and attachments to execution-core provenance and show shadow-screening agreement stats to admins. (b) Parse shell commands into a syntax tree before capability policy, with an org floor (deny, approve) and typed reason codes. (c) Route elevated-risk browser actions into the room's approval card with decision ids. (d) Mask every injected credential value (raw, URL-encoded, base64 variants) in tool output before it reaches the model or the room. (e) Apply pii_filter and secret masking to agent-authored room messages before append, and optionally to human messages as DLP.
whyItMatters: In a multi-human room, colleagues' messages and shared files are untrusted input to someone's personal agent, and agent output posted to a room is a new leak path for credentials and personal data. The building blocks exist, so most of this is wiring them to the Space.

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Injection screening with provenance: 1 of 5 (qm); command policy: 2 of 5 (qm, grokbot); secret and PII redaction: 4 of 5 (table-stakes); inline DLP: 1 of 5 (teams).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Tag every content chunk with provenance (owner, member, external, tool), screen external chunks with deterministic markers plus a classifier under a deadline, quarantine on enforce, and keep verdicts without payloads so a candidate rubric can be replayed. Commands are parsed with tree-sitter-bash into simple commands and redirects, evaluated against an org floor, and return allow, ask or deny with a reason code. Value-based masking precomputes needles for every injected secret (raw, URI-encoded, base64, base64url, ignoring very short ones) and masks stdout, stderr and errors; pattern redaction covers bearer, JWT, sk-, AWS keys, PEM and DSN userinfo.

title: Files become agent input and room knowledge: per-turn re-authorized attachments as model input, extraction with summaries and typed refusals, and agent-proposed pinned knowledge

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: [R-t1-01-07] A room has no attachment path, so nothing reaches the model; the Chat documents and extract routes exist but are not reused in Space. [R-t1-08-07] Knowledge reaches room agents through the read-only Space retrieval binding and nobody can add knowledge from inside the room. There is no auto-summary, no typed upload refusal and no Space-level retention. approachOriginal: [R-t1-01-07] Model Plane (session-core prompt builder): gather attachment refs from entries in scope, ask the Data Plane documents/retrieval API (no cross-plane DB reads) to authorize each ref for the invoking subject on every turn, then pick native file input or extracted text from a per-provider route table; Data Plane owns extraction with heap/time limits (the Chat extract route is the starting point); emit notices for skipped or truncated files; wrap as untrusted data; persist references only. Optional later: pre-caption staged files, with delete-on-discard and a ZDR consent rule. [R-t1-08-07] Data Plane: on room upload (F-t1-013 (R-t1-08-03)) run extraction and index into the Space retrieval binding; a Model Plane job writes the summary back as a Data Plane field computed only within viewer-authorized scope; add a typed refusal enum to the upload response. For crystallization, reuse wiki-store SubmitProposal and ReviewProposal: a room agent submits a proposal against the canvas page or a knowledge page, Application holds the approval item, a human with wiki.approve accepts, and the result becomes a new version with source_refs provenance. Frontend: summary card on the file and a proposal review surface patterned on the Operating Map review. Under ZDR keep only a session extract.

title: Webhooks that wake room agents (Space-bound inbound endpoints)
summary: Let a Space manager create a secret webhook endpoint bound to a room and an agent. Ingestion Plane verifies the provider or HMAC signature, dedups the delivery, filters by JSON path and caps the payload; Model Plane capability-core then receives a wake envelope on the same trigger path schedules use, with the payload wrapped as untrusted data, and Control Plane decides every fire under the endpoint owner's authority.
whyItMatters: It turns room agents from chat-only into event-driven coworkers: a GitHub PR, a Stripe dispute or a monitoring alert starts work in the room. The agent-centric references that have it (qm, buzz) treat it as the way agents are triggered by the outside world, and it reuses the schedule fire path Verevon already governs. The same unattended-turn plumbing also unblocks per-agent email (F-t1-075 (R-t1-06-10)).

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 5 sources; differentiator (webhook triggers also appear in Slack/Teams workflow builders)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: qm's WebhookReceiver.deliver(id, headers, rawBody) runs a per-provider verifier (github, slack, stripe, linear, generic HMAC) with constant-time compare, handles provider handshakes, derives a delivery id for dedup, filters events by JSON path (e.g. action in [opened]), caps the payload at 16,000 chars in a wake envelope, wraps it as untrusted content and dispatches it like a cron fire under the endpoint owner's authority. The secret is shown once; each endpoint has an event log. Buzz adds outbound calls with SSRF protection.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: The baseline recorded 'absent' after searching only the Spaces router and Convex schema; this pass found more (SRC). integration-corev2 already receives org-level provider webhooks at /api/v1/webhooks/:provider (signature check, normalise, tenant resolution, stored with a duplicate flag, published as verevon.ingestion.integration.webhook_received on NATS), and the only consumer found is conversation-core's inbox. Missing for Spaces: per-room secret endpoints (the route only accepts providers in the fixed catalogue), generic HMAC and GitHub/Stripe/Linear-style verifiers with path filters and a payload cap, a consumer that turns the event into a Control-decided capability-core fire bound to space_ref, and any UI. bridge-core's outbound webhook adapter (durable, retrying) is not wired to Spaces.

approachOriginal: Ingestion Plane integration-corev2: add a space-webhook route family (endpoint id in the path) backed by an endpoint record owned by Control (secret shown once, space_ref, agent binding, filter, size cap, owner), reuse the existing verify, normalise, dedup and store path, and publish a wake event carrying only a reference (as webhook_received does, with the stored payload fetched by id). Model Plane capability-core: consume the event as a trigger variant beside schedules, obtain a Control fire decision per delivery (owner authority, privacy/ZDR claims), then start an unattended turn through the Space scheduled-run machinery with the payload wrapped as untrusted content. Frontend: endpoint management and a delivery log in the Agent or Work tab; results post into the room. ZDR rooms keep payloads out of retention. Outbound calls (agent or workflow calling external URLs) can reuse bridge-core's webhook adapter once its SSRF/egress controls are confirmed (INF).

The woken run is tool-free and bounded today and S4.1 itself says scheduled effects are not yet safe, so the first release can only summarise the payload into the room. Payloads are attacker-controlled: carry them as unscreened content, never with tool access in the same turn. ZDR rooms must drop payloads. Delivery of the result (S4.4) is unbuilt.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Model the endpoint as a webhook/connector-event source kind of the S4.3 watch primitive (Space and member authority, bounded predicate, cursor, untrusted trust level) instead of a new trigger variant beside schedules; keep the integration-corev2 endpoint-id route family and secret handling. Add a Control shared-room fire decision first (critical path). Ship notify-and-summarise through the tool-free scheduled lane, and gate tool use on S4.1 effects closing. Do not state that Control decides every fire as if it already works for rooms.
verevon.effortNote: Was M and marked a quick win. A Control decision kind for shared rooms, an endpoint record, a Model-side trigger, payload trust handling and UI make it L; it is not a quick win.
verevon.verdictReason: The org-level receive/verify/dedup half exists and the plan overlaps S4.3, but the claimed wake path rests on Control and runtime pieces that exist only for personal Spaces and tool-free runs.
